analysis: The supplied units are BASE-side excerpts (lines 326-582 and 583-954) of docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. They contain the prefix-cache capability/telemetry, heartbeat, inference response, attestation_response and models_replace protocol descriptions. The patch shown is documentation only: it bumps the "Last updated" date (line 3) and extends the GLM5Next reasoning-control table row around lines 1147-1155 with `reasoning: null` handling and `reasoning.summary`/`reasoning.generate_summary` no-op values (`auto`, `concise`, `detailed`), while refusing other `reasoning` members. No code, wire schema, authorization, attestation, encryption or cache-storage behavior changes in the visible hunks, so I identified no security regression. The reviewed text is consistent with existing threat-model assumptions: T-041/A-001 (prefix-cache telemetry is observational and contains no prompt text, token IDs or cache keys), T-008 (E2E-encrypted chunks), T-053 (service reservation and authorization lifecycle) and TB-002 (provider-supplied fields are sanitized or clamped by the coordinator). Limits: the head side of the changed lines (1147-1155) was not supplied as a numbered unit, and the patch excerpt is truncated. I could not verify that the accompanying GLM5NextPromptPolicy.swift change correctly refuses unknown `reasoning` members, so the documented behavior is unconfirmed. Any source change should be checked for fail-closed validation, since lax acceptance of unknown controls could be a prompt-handling regression. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.
